decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: Recent data suggest that growth rates of household spending and business fixed investment have moderated from their strong fourth-quarter readings.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that household and business spending slowed down compared to the very strong fourth quarter.

changes.quote: The economic outlook has strengthened in recent months.
changes.explanation: Committee members feel more confident about the direction of the overall economy.

changes.quote: Inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to move up in coming months and to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term.
changes.explanation: The timeline for inflation reaching the 2 percent target was shifted slightly from "this year" to "in coming months."

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The official decision was made to increase interest rates due to strong job markets and steady inflation progress.

changes.quote: Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Loretta J. Mester; Randal K. Quarles; and John C. Williams.
changes.explanation: Jerome H. Powell led his first policy vote as Chairman with unanimous support from the Committee.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate.
The economic outlook has strengthened in recent months.
On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have continued to run below 2 percent.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.16% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.89% and moved 0 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.46% would not change.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 227k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.3% over the past year (February 2018); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.18%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.46% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve plans to continue gradually raising interest rates as long as the economy remains on its current path. Educational forecast models suggest a hold is most likely at the next meeting with a 71 percent probability, compared to a 29 percent chance of a hike.
